text:
alexa (support): FYI customer AcmeCorp on Dedicated reporting a sudden throughput drop this morning. Was ~560 rps, now 60-90 rps, lots of 429s and 1.5-2s token latencies. They say it started ~08:57 UTC.

matt (eng-runtime): thanks — any logs or examples from their side? 429 suggests throttling but could be inefficient batching.

alexa (support): pasted what they sent: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":2048}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` getting repeated `HTTP 429 {"error":"throttle"}` and `latency=1200ms token=1`.

devon (sre): grabbing metrics for dedicated pool id=ded-az1-17 now. autoscaler-bot, did we see scale actions around 08:50-09:10?

autoscaler-bot: No scale-up events in window 08:30-09:30 UTC for pool ded-az1-17. Current replicas=4, min=2, max=12. CPU low, but queue_depth metric: 0→peaked at 1200 pending->sustained 300.

matt (eng-runtime): queue_depth + high pending with low CPU is classic continuous-batcher headway problem — microbursts with long per-request token counts create small batches, headway waits add up. What is `max_batch_tokens` on that pool?

rebecca (infra): policy shows `max_batch_tokens: 4096` on the model shim, but there's a per-deployment override `max_batch_tokens: 512` applied in canary config rolled at 08:42.

ingrid (cs): customer says they didn't change anything on their side. We rolled a canary earlier for scheduling heuristics this morning — could that be it?

matt (eng-runtime): yep — the canary lowered max_batch_tokens to reduce tail latency for short requests, but with this customer's workload (many long contexts) it fragments batches and increases headway. That explains sustained queue even though pods not CPU-bound.

alexa (support): customer is asking for repro steps so they can validate after we change things.

devon (sre): quick repro for internal: run loadgen with mixed token lengths: `python loadgen.py --rps 600 --p50_tokens 1200 --p90_tokens 1800 --duration 300 --api-key X --endpoint /v1/generate` you'll see batch sizes drop to 1-2 and queue grows.

matt (eng-runtime): mitigation plan: 1) roll back canary override `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 for pool ded-az1-17, 2) bump scheduler headway target to 15ms, 3) short rolling restart of 1 pod to pick up config.

rebecca (infra): I'm prepping the rollback now. ETA 8 minutes. Will annotate deploy with `#inc:1767894321 headway rollback for AcmeCorp`.

autoscaler-bot: rollback started for config canary-2026-03-17-08:42 on pool ded-az1-17.

matt (eng-runtime): also leaving note to tune fairness: reduce per-tenant max_pending_tokens to avoid single tenant starving others if they send huge requests.

ingrid (cs): telling AcmeCorp we plan rollback and will follow up with repro commands they can run.

rebecca (infra): rollback complete at 08:58 UTC, pods picked up config.

autoscaler-bot: Observed queue_depth drop from 300→40 over 90s. No additional scale actions.

alexa (support): AcmeCorp ran quick smoke — reported throughput back to ~520 rps, 429s gone. They will run a longer soak this afternoon.

matt (eng-runtime): follow-ups: (a) add canary guard to reject `max_batch_tokens` reductions for pools with heavy long-context workload, (b) add a dashboard alert when queue_depth > X while CPU < Y, (c) add a repro job for microburst workload we can run on CI.

devon (sre): I'll file the incident ticket with timeline and link to loadgen script.

ingrid (cs): noted — I'll schedule a postmortem with AcmeCorp and share learnings. :white_check_mark:

rebecca (infra): thanks team — closing thread once postmortem ticket created.

alexa (support): closing note: customer happy for now. will reopen if regression. :thumbsup:
